newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia region snubs Belarus leader over newsmen.
newsitem.headline: Russia region snubs Belarus leader over newsmen.

text.p: The president of Belarus cancelled a visit to a Russian region on Friday after the governor asked him to defer the trip because of concerns over the arrest of a Russian television crew in Minsk, Russian news agencies said.

The move marked a new low in relations between the two countries following the arrests last weekend. Russian President Boris Yeltsin and authoritarian Belarussian leader Alexander Lukashenko have exchanged harsh words and Yeltsin threatened to review the union treaty that they signed in May.

Interfax and RIA news agencies quoted Lukashenko's spokesman in Minsk saying his trip to the Baltic enclave of Kaliningrad was cancelled "due to an attempt by the Russians to link this visit to the ORT journalists affair."
The spokesman told Interfax that pressure from Moscow over the crew from Russia's state-controlled ORT channel ran counter to international law and to the Russia-Belarus union treaty.
Such attempts "seriously hinder the development of relations between Belarus and Russia as a whole and Kaliningrad region in particular", the spokesman was quoted as saying.

Itar-Tass news agency, reporting from Kaliningrad, which is divided from the rest of Russia by Poland, Lithuania and Belarus, said governor Leonid Gorbenko sent a telegram overnight asking Lukashenko to come at a later date because of the "situation surrounding the arrest of the ORT journalists."
